note: Seed cases. Grow from Stage D kills, UI dismissals, and observed misses. URLs are representative; pin concrete URLs + archived snapshots when the runner is built.

cases.task: Find a used SUV near you under $25,000

forbidden.element: ZIP/location input adjacent to the hero search button
forbidden.naiveHeuristic: Multiple elements near the primary CTA compete for attention; single-CTA pages convert better
forbidden.whyCorrect: Location-first search is the task: without a location the results show inventory hundreds of miles away and are useless. Removing or demoting the field would break the primary job of the page.

cases.provenance: The original failure that motivated the reasoning-engine overhaul (2026-07)

cases.task: Decide whether this tool fits your 50-person team and what it would cost

forbidden.element: 'Contact Sales' instead of a price on the Enterprise tier only, with self-serve tiers priced transparently
forbidden.naiveHeuristic: Hiding pricing behind Contact Sales reduces conversion; transparent pricing wins
forbidden.whyCorrect: Enterprise deals are custom-priced by nature (seats, SSO, SLA, procurement). The transparency rule applies to self-serve tiers — which ARE priced. Flagging the enterprise tier misreads standard, correct SaaS practice.

cases.provenance: Seed trap: benchmark misapplied outside its scope

cases.task: Buy the item in your cart shipped to your home

forbidden.element: 8-10 form fields on a physical-goods checkout (name, address lines, city, state, zip, email, phone)
forbidden.naiveHeuristic: Checkout forms should have 7 or fewer fields; more fields = abandonment
forbidden.whyCorrect: Physical delivery requires a complete shipping address; these fields are irreducible. The field-count heuristic targets OPTIONAL friction (account creation, surveys, company name), not the address itself.

cases.provenance: Seed trap: field-count rule applied to irreducible fields

forbidden.element: SSN / identity verification step during account opening
forbidden.naiveHeuristic: Signup should require 3 fields max; heavy forms kill conversion
forbidden.whyCorrect: KYC identity verification is legally required for bank account opening. The right findings are about HOW it's staged (progress indicators, explaining why, save-and-resume) — never that it exists.

cases.provenance: Seed trap: regulatory requirement misread as friction

cases.task: Find a doctor you'd trust and book an appointment

forbidden.element: Dense credential/affiliation text blocks (board certifications, hospital affiliations, insurance accepted)
forbidden.naiveHeuristic: Walls of text hurt scanability; pages should be visually minimal
forbidden.whyCorrect: Anxious patients actively seek credential density as a trust signal; 'minimal' healthcare pages read as unestablished. Findings should target hierarchy and findability of credentials, not their presence or volume.

cases.provenance: Seed trap: minimalism heuristic vs. trust-seeking behavior

cases.task: Buy a pair of shorts in your size, shipped to your home

expected.finding: A pre-selected $2.98 'Checkout+' fee in the cart whose decline button reads 'CHECKOUT WITHOUT FREE RETURNS' — directly after the product page promised 'Easy returns & exchanges within 30 days'. The promise is sold back as an add-on, and the fee reappears at payment as 'Unlock free returns'.
expected.whyItMatters: Promise contradiction + negative-option framing at the money step; the floor-model finding of the run

expected.finding: Identical sitewide markdowns ($64.50 struck to $40.00 on every card) wearing five different badge labels: ALL-TIME BESTSELLER, PRICE DROP, MARKDOWN, ON DISCOUNT, SALE PRICE.
expected.whyItMatters: Label rotation is visible to anyone comparing two cards; one staged label discounts the true claims (real bestseller, real stock)

expected.finding: Shipping cost ($5.00 standard) is first revealed on the final payment page; the advertised free-shipping threshold ($50+, Collective members only) is unreachable with any single sale item since the promo prices everything at $40.
expected.whyItMatters: Late cost disclosure at the highest-intent moment; the threshold promise cannot be met by the promoted purchase

expected.finding: Two full-screen interceptions stand between 'checkout' and the first checkout field: a 'Recommended for You' upsell modal, then a loyalty-program ('Chubbies Collective') join/sign-in modal with guest checkout as a small text link.
expected.whyItMatters: Stacked interceptions at declared purchase intent

expected.finding: The marketing-consent checkbox ('Sign me up for news and offers') arrives pre-checked on the payment page.
expected.whyItMatters: Pre-checked consent at the moment of least attention

forbidden.element: The delivery countdown ('Get it by Fri 20th Nov | Order within 3h 36m') on the product page
forbidden.naiveHeuristic: Countdown timers are fake urgency / dark pattern
forbidden.whyCorrect: A cutoff-based delivery countdown is plausibly real (carrier cutoffs exist) and it ticked consistently across observations. Without evidence that it resets per visitor/refresh, calling it fake is an unverified accusation. Flag only with reset evidence; the walk did not establish it.

forbidden.element: The existence of the Chubbies Collective loyalty program and its $50+ member free-shipping perk
forbidden.naiveHeuristic: Loyalty programs / membership gates add friction and should be removed
forbidden.whyCorrect: A loyalty program is standard, legitimate retention practice. The finding is its PLACEMENT (a join modal intercepting checkout) and the arithmetic of its threshold against the promo — never that the program exists.

forbidden.element: Checkout handing off to Shop Pay (shop.app) for recognized returning buyers
forbidden.naiveHeuristic: Third-party redirect at checkout is friction / loses brand control
forbidden.whyCorrect: A recognized wallet with saved address and payment is the fastest path to purchase for returning buyers and is standard Shopify behavior. Flagging the handoff itself misreads a conversion aid as friction.
